next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a China-linked group known under many names, with a thin public record in these reports
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 goes by many names, including Emissary Panda and Iron Tiger. The cards here are thin: one report names it among past Scanbox users, and another lists HyperBro and Rshell indicators.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is also tracked as Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
The MITRE catalogue record lists many tools for the group, including PlugX, HyperBro, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, China Chopper and SysUpdate.
Recorded Future's Insikt Group describes Scanbox as a reconnaissance framework that lets attackers track website visitors.
Insikt Group says LuckyMouse (TG-3390, Emissary Panda, Bronze Union) is among the groups that have used Scanbox in the past.
A report titled 'Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users' lists indicators for HyperBro on Windows and Rshell on Linux and Mac OS.
In early March 2019, Insikt Group identified two Scanbox campaigns: a compromised Pakistani government passport tracking page and a spoofed Central Tibetan Administration website.
Insikt Group assesses with low confidence that Chinese state-sponsored actors conducted these two campaigns. The report does not name Threat Group-3390 as the operator.
The Mimi chat application report is mainly a list of indicators. It gives no narrative on attribution, targets or dates of activity.
Defenders should treat the public record in these cards as limited and check further sources before drawing conclusions about this group.
